title: English Practice Quiz 0952
description: A ten-question English practice quiz covering grammar, vocabulary and practical communication.

questions.question: A customer says a product is faulty. You should first ___.
options: listen and ask for relevant details
promise a refund without checking policy
questions.explanation: Listening and gathering facts is the first step towards a fair response.

questions.question: A 'replacement' is an item provided ___.
questions.explanation: A replacement takes the place of the original item.

questions.question: Which response is best when you do not know an answer?
options: I will confirm the information and get back to you.
Ask someone else and stop speaking.
questions.explanation: It is better to verify information than provide an unreliable answer.

questions.question: A customer who returns regularly is often called a ___.
questions.explanation: A repeat customer makes purchases or uses a service more than once.

questions.question: To 'escalate' a complaint means to ___.
options: refer it to a higher level for attention
send it to an unrelated customer
questions.explanation: Escalation passes an issue to someone with greater authority or expertise.

questions.question: A service guarantee is a promise about ___.
options: the standard or remedy a provider will offer
questions.explanation: A guarantee describes a provider's commitment under stated conditions.

questions.question: Which phrase is suitable after resolving a customer's issue?
options: Thank you for bringing this to our attention.
questions.explanation: This acknowledges the customer and closes the interaction courteously.

questions.question: A customer's feedback can help an organisation ___.
questions.explanation: Feedback can reveal strengths and areas needing improvement.

questions.question: A 'courtesy call' is generally made as a gesture of ___.
questions.explanation: A courtesy call is made to maintain helpful communication.

questions.question: When explaining a service charge, staff should ___.
options: state the amount and what it covers clearly
give different amounts to different people without reason
questions.explanation: Clear explanations help customers understand what they are paying for.
